task: C6 follow-up — Jaw taken out of the D2/D3/D4 gain solve; the authored mouth restored in the shipped GLB

defect.summary: The gain passes amplify every rotation channel about its own bind rotation. `Jaw` is neither PROTECTED nor PANEL_COUPLED, so the mouth was amplified with the rig: attack 32.0->176.9deg (5.53x), attack2 24.0->53.7deg (2.24x), death 50.0->179.1deg (3.58x). A jaw cannot open 177deg, so the shipped pose is not a stronger bite, it is an inverted one.
defect.localisedBy: breath, attackAir2 and idle were never gain-passed and agree with the blend to 0.0000deg, so the divergence is the gain pass and not the export.

exportRelation.why: The exporter writes the frame-0 pose as the node TRS, not the armature-rest pose. `rest_glb * basis(k)` is off by the constant basis(0), which for this rig is the C6 compensation of 2.090deg.

dynamics.note: Free: the jaw never holds a frame's maximum angular rate here, so the restore changes no digit of the metric.

coupledSet.note: The membrane panels must move as one set, so the coupled group shares one gain computed from its worst member; that member is already past the cap, so the whole set is left untouched.

restoreOnly.note: p95 560 < floor 734.2 and mean 305 < floor 351.8. The mouth set the maximum in 158 of 240 frames.

rejectedAlternatives.evidence: The shipped clip already carries 21 bones more than 150deg from bind (R_Thigh 179.1deg, every WingD* panel 179.3deg). qpow past 180deg wraps the short way, so gain 1.8 turns a 179deg bone into -38deg: it inverts the pose. It measures best of all (mean 512, 102% of V1) and is still wrong.
The accel ceiling binds at about 1.05x (accel 48588 > 46128 at 1.1x) while p95 needs about 1.31x (560 -> 734). Contradiction.

All 10 Tail* channels match GROUPS.tail and ripple() returns non-null, but the tail never holds a per-frame maximum: 2..14deg at 2..4 cycles changes no digit of the metric (p95 560, mean 305 throughout).
Clears at p95 764 against the 734 floor — a 3.9% margin chosen to clear a floor rather than to make the clip better.
Smoothing buys the accel headroom a bare gain cannot, and takes the peak from 1738 to 1383 for no other reason (gain 1.8, 2 passes).

probe.note: `wrapped` is computed from the pre-gain excursion, not from the built pose: a shortest-arc angle can never exceed 180deg, so once qpow wraps the measurement reads `360 - gain*excursion` and the instrument that produced it can no longer see the wrap.
probe.reading: A uniform gain does not fix death at any size: at 1.05x it already wraps 20 bones and still fails, and at 1.8x it reaches V1's p95/mean while wrapping 24 bones to 322.7deg (i.e. -37.3deg, an inverted pose) and blowing the accel ceiling (68,544 against 54,819). The capped row wraps nothing and keeps the shipped peak and accel.

hinge.note: Re-measured with tools/blender/recenter_v2_jaw_pivot.mjs after the restore. The hinge stays exactly lateral and every clip now opens to its authored amplitude.

gates.checkProvenance: passed — blend stage C6, NOT export-safe
gates.aliases: all three shipped GLBs byte-identical at f5d768a2…

warnings: attack passes its dynamics gate with a 0.5% margin (mean 1664.3 against a 1673.7 ceiling, i.e. 139.3% of V1's 1194.8). Pre-existing and unchanged by this pass: the jaw never holds a frame maximum there, so the restore moves nothing. The risk is that attack is more energetic than V1, not less.
idempotent: Re-running `--write` after the pass reports "nothing to write — every clip already carries its authored jaw". The compensation is only ever applied as part of a jaw restore, so there is nothing left to re-apply.
determinismCheck: Two independent runs both land on f5d768a2…, 6,738,692 B from 04dbda5c… — the pass is byte-deterministic. Separately, the C6 asset was reproduced from git HEAD (b5f1c1ef…) with recenter_v2_jaw_pivot.mjs --write and came back byte-identical at 04dbda5c…, 6,738,716 B, which re-confirms that pass independently.
